key_insight: Diffusion-based anomaly detection can identify fatal cerebral hemorrhage on postmortem brain CT, and weak image-level supervision performs best.
clinical_relevance: This could support faster forensic triage of postmortem CT scans by highlighting likely hemorrhage cases for expert review.
method: Retrospective PMCT dataset: 265 healthy subjects and 33 fatal intracranial hemorrhage cases.
Applied automated brain extraction, slice selection, and intensity normalization.
Trained two diffusion models: unsupervised AnoDDPM and a weakly supervised classifier-guided model.
evidence_signal: On image-level evaluation, AnoDDPM achieved AUROC 0.928 and AUPRC 0.794, while the classifier-guided model improved to AUROC 0.991 and AUPRC 0.960, with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data with limited hemorrhage cases may affect generalizability and real-world performance across scanners, protocols, and decomposed postmortem anatomy.
paper_title: 2D anomaly detection of fatal cerebral hemorrhage on postmortem CT
